The proposed framework uses a data-driven approach to learn touch exploration strategies.
High-resolution vision-based tactile sensors are used in the proposed framework.
The Chamfer distance is used as a distance metric to measure the similarity between predicted and target surfaces.
Over 25k CAD models from the ABC dataset are used for training and evaluation.
50 grasps are uniformly placed around the 3D object in the active touch exploration framework.
A chart-based approach using a graph convolutional network (GCN) and a vision CNN is used for shape reconstruction.
Two GCNs are used in the shape reconstruction model, one for learning an object prior and the other for refining the object belief.
A mesh autoencoder is used to produce a learned embeddings space for dimensionality reduction.
A 2-step deformation process is used to refine the object belief in the mesh deformation process.
Data-driven policies are used to select the positions of the next touches to acquire in the touch exploration framework.
Euclidean distance in the embeddings space is used as a distance metric to compare predicted shapes.
The proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art results in 3D shape reconstruction accuracy.
The framework is evaluated on a dataset of over 25k CAD models from the ABC dataset.
The proposed framework is designed to be extensible to other modalities and applications.
The framework uses a combination of vision and touch signals to improve shape reconstruction accuracy.
